transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Yeah, thank you. Well, I'm here because things have just completely fallen apart at work, and I mean, it’s entirely my own doing, which is the most frustrating part of all of this. I’m an industrial production manager, so my job is always demanding, I have a master's degree, I'm used to high-stress environments, but recently I just went into this absolute... overdrive, I guess you'd call it. 

I went from my normal baseline to suddenly launching nonstop plant redesign projects. Like, I decided out of nowhere that we needed to overhaul the entire assembly floor layout because the efficiency metrics were off by maybe a fraction of a percent. Usually, that isn't a crisis, but I felt this intense, overpowering need to fix it right that second. So I was drawing up these massive schematics, and then I was calling our suppliers way after hours. I mean, I was dialing vendors at two or three in the morning, leaving them these incredibly long, detailed voicemails about supply chain logistics and demanding expedited shipping on raw materials we didn't even need for another quarter. 

And on top of all that, I completely scrapped our existing HR software and spent I don't even know how many hours rewriting the entire shift plan for my whole department by myself. I was just color-coding every single fifteen-minute interval for over a hundred employees because I was convinced I had unlocked this perfect, flawless system that was going to revolutionize our output. 

But then... and this is why I finally made the appointment... it just stopped. Like hitting a concrete wall. I went from doing all of that, running a million miles an hour and feeling like I could do the work of ten executives, to suddenly being completely unable to keep up with the very plans I had just set in motion. The new shift plan is active, the suppliers are calling me back asking for purchase orders, the floor redesign is half-finished and causing bottlenecks, and I can barely even bring myself to open my email, let alone manage the teams I just reorganized. It’s like I built this massive, complicated machine and then completely lost the ability to operate it, and the backlog is just piling up, and I just... I don't understand how I could go from being so incredibly capable and driven to just completely paralyzed like this.

Before this recent period of high energy, have you ever had episodes—lasting days or weeks—where you felt unusually depressed, low, or lacking energy, or previous times where you felt this same kind of intense high energy?

Well, as for the high energy, maybe I've had smaller bursts before, like when I was finishing my master's thesis or pushing through a big quarter, but nothing quite this extreme or destructive. But the low part... the depressed, lacking energy part you mentioned? That is exactly where I am right now, and it's honestly unbearable. 

Lately I wake up in the temporary apartment I'm staying in—which is just this sterile, corporate-furnished place because my actual townhouse is having massive plumbing work done, which is a whole separate logistical nightmare I don't even have the bandwidth to deal with right now—but I wake up there, and I just have this... this heavy, hollow feeling. It just sits right in the middle of my chest. It's like the day is already completely ruined before I even get out of bed, before I even drive to the plant. 

And the drive is only fifteen minutes, but just the thought of putting the key in the ignition makes that hollow feeling so much worse. I just lie there in this strange bed, staring at the ceiling, feeling like I weigh a thousand pounds. It's not just being tired from working too hard or staying up late calling vendors, it's this deep, empty weight where I can't even see the point of trying to fix the mess I made. I just feel so incredibly low, like you said, from the absolute second I open my eyes, and I can't seem to shake it no matter how much I tell myself I need to get up and go manage my team.
During that period of intense energy and nonstop activity, about how many days in a row did it last before it stopped?

Well, the high energy part... I guess it was building up for a bit, but the really intense part, the overdrive where I was doing all the redesigns and calling people in the middle of the night, that lasted for... oh, I don't know, maybe four or five days? A week at the absolute most. It's honestly a blur of just constant, frantic motion. But the shift... that horrible crash from feeling like a superhero to barely being able to function at all? That has been going on since I moved into this temporary apartment. 

Which, like I said, was about three weeks ago. Three weeks of waking up in that awful, beige room with the terrible abstract art on the walls, just feeling completely paralyzed. And it's so frustrating because I know exactly when it started, right around the time the movers dropped off my rented furniture. I remember sitting on the edge of this couch that isn't mine, surrounded by boxes of files I had brought home from the plant, and suddenly realizing I couldn't bring myself to open a single one of them. And it's been exactly like that every single day for the last three weeks. Just this complete, heavy stop.

During that week of intense energy, did your behavior cause serious problems that others noticed—like a coworker, supervisor, or family member stepping in, or anyone suggesting you needed urgent help or hospitalization?

Well, hospitalization? No, no one said anything like that, but... but yes, people definitely noticed, and it definitely caused serious problems. I mean, it was impossible *not* to notice, considering how I was acting. 

There was this one specific meeting... it was supposed to be a standard, routine shift-planning meeting with the other department heads. Normally, I run those meetings, I have the agenda, I keep everyone on track. But this time, I came in with all those color-coded charts I mentioned, and I was just talking so fast, completely talking over the floor supervisors, telling them how everything they were doing was wrong and how my new system was going to fix it all. I was just pacing back and forth in the conference room, and I remember looking at their faces and they were just staring at me. Not even arguing, just staring. 

And then... I don't even know how it happened, but my brain just sort of short-circuited in the middle of trying to explain the supply chain logistics. I just lost my train of thought completely, and I felt this overwhelming rush of panic because I realized I couldn't actually make the schedule work with the raw materials we had. And I just... I had to ask to be pulled out of the meeting. I literally stopped mid-sentence, grabbed my charts, and told my assistant I had to leave. I just walked out. 

And because of that, because I just abandoned this critical planning session, occupational health actually got involved. My supervisor pulled me aside later that afternoon—well, tried to, I was frantically trying to reorganize the breakroom at that point—and said they were seriously concerned because I wasn't able to carry out the basic production decisions that my entire role depends on. Like, I couldn't even approve the weekly overtime budget because I was too busy obsessing over the exact placement of the safety tape on the assembly floor. So, yeah, it was bad. They didn't say hospital, but they definitely knew something was very, very wrong with me, and it completely disrupted the whole plant's operations for the week.

During these past three weeks of feeling low and paralyzed, have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things that others don't see, or having strong beliefs that others tell you aren't true—such as feeling certain you're being punished or that you've caused irreversible harm?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I'm definitely not hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there. The apartment is just... it's just quiet. Too quiet, really, except for the hum of the refrigerator, which is this awful, persistent noise that I fixate on when I'm lying there unable to move. But no voices. 

And as for beliefs... I mean, I don't think I'm being punished by some outside force, if that's what you mean. I know exactly why I'm in this situation. It's because of my own actions during that week where I lost my mind and ruined everything at work. I don't have some delusion that the universe is out to get me or anything. It's just... it's just the crushing reality of what I actually did. 

Like, I know I messed up the production schedule. That's a fact, not a strong belief that people are telling me isn't true. My supervisor literally told me I messed it up. And I know I alienated my team when I talked over them in that meeting. I can still see their faces, you know? Just staring at me. That's real. That's not me imagining things. 

So, no, I'm not disconnected from reality like that. If anything, the reality of what I've done is just so intensely clear to me right now, and that's exactly why I feel so heavy and paralyzed. I just lie there thinking about all the very real, very tangible things I broke—relationships at the plant, my reputation, the actual workflow of the assembly floor—and it's just... it's just a mountain of my own making. But it's all real. No voices, no hallucinations, nothing like that at all. Just me and the mess I made.
During these past three weeks of feeling this heavy and paralyzed, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or wishing you weren't alive?

No, no, I haven't... I mean, I haven't made any plans to hurt myself or anything like that. I don't want to die. It's not that I want to stop existing entirely, it's just... it's more like I just want the overwhelming weight of everything to stop. I want to wake up in that beige apartment and not immediately feel like I'm drowning in regret and exhaustion. 

But actually wanting to end my life? No. I haven't had thoughts like that. Even when I'm lying there, staring at that awful abstract painting for hours on end, listening to the refrigerator hum, and feeling completely incapable of even sitting up to open a file box... even then, my brain doesn't go to suicide. It just goes to this loop of everything I've ruined. I just think about the plant, and the production schedules, and my supervisor's face, and how I'm going to fix it all when I can't even get off the couch. 

It's a miserable feeling, this complete paralysis. It's like being trapped in your own body while your mind just forces you to watch a highlight reel of your worst mistakes. But as heavy as it is, and as much as I wish I could just hit a pause button on my brain and get some relief from the guilt and the exhaustion, I haven't ever thought about hurting myself to make it stop. I just... I just want to feel normal again. I want to be able to go back to work and run a meeting without completely losing my mind or abandoning my team. I just want to be the person I was before all this started, you know? But no, no thoughts of hurting myself. Just... just stuck. Really, really stuck.

Over these past three weeks, has the low mood affected your ability to manage basic daily self-care—like eating regular meals, bathing, or getting dressed—or have you still been able to keep up with those things despite feeling low?

Basic self-care... yeah, that’s... that’s pretty much gone out the window. I mean, getting dressed? I think I’ve been wearing the same oversized grey sweatpants since Tuesday. Or maybe Monday. Showering just feels like this impossible, monumental task. Just the thought of standing under the water and having to, you know, actually wash my hair and go through the motions... it’s just too much. I just can't bring myself to do it. 

But the eating... my eating is just completely all over the place right now. I used to be so regimented, you know? Meal prep on Sundays, perfectly portioned lunches for the plant so I could eat while reviewing the shift logs. But now, it’s like my body doesn't even know what a normal routine is anymore. Some days, I’ll be lying there on the couch, just paralyzed, staring at the ceiling and listening to that awful refrigerator hum, and I’ll happen to glance at my phone and realize it’s 4 p.m. and I haven’t had a single bite of food. I’ll realize that all I’ve had is coffee. Just... maybe a cup or two of coffee that I forced myself to make in the morning, which usually just end up sitting on the coffee table getting cold anyway. 

And then, it’s like a switch flips, but not in a good way. Other nights, I’ll just... I'll end up ordering a massive amount of Chinese food or something, because the idea of actually turning on the stove or chopping a vegetable is just laughable right now. And when the delivery gets here, I don't even bother getting a plate or sitting down at the table like a normal person. I just stand there, right in the middle of the kitchen, under those terrible fluorescent lights, eating the takeout straight from the container. And the weirdest part is, I’m not even really hungry when I’m doing it. I'm just standing there, mindlessly chewing, staring at the backsplash, while my brain is still just agonizing over the assembly floor and the overtime budget and all the people I let down. It's not about nourishment at all, it's just this mechanical thing I do while I'm trapped in my own head. So, no, regular meals aren't happening. None of it is happening. I can barely manage to keep track of what day it is, let alone actually take care of myself.

patient.answer:
No, no, I haven't... I mean, I haven't made any plans to hurt myself or anything like that. I don't want to die. It's not that I want to stop existing entirely, it's just... it's more like I just want the overwhelming weight of everything to stop. I want to wake up in that beige apartment and not immediately feel like I'm drowning in regret and exhaustion. 

But actually wanting to end my life? No. I haven't had thoughts like that. Even when I'm lying there, staring at that awful abstract painting for hours on end, listening to the refrigerator hum, and feeling completely incapable of even sitting up to open a file box... even then, my brain doesn't go to suicide. It just goes to this loop of everything I've ruined. I just think about the plant, and the production schedules, and my supervisor's face, and how I'm going to fix it all when I can't even get off the couch. 

It's a miserable feeling, this complete paralysis. It's like being trapped in your own body while your mind just forces you to watch a highlight reel of your worst mistakes. But as heavy as it is, and as much as I wish I could just hit a pause button on my brain and get some relief from the guilt and the exhaustion, I haven't ever thought about hurting myself to make it stop. I just... I just want to feel normal again. I want to be able to go back to work and run a meeting without completely losing my mind or abandoning my team. I just want to be the person I was before all this started, you know? But no, no thoughts of hurting myself. Just... just stuck. Really, really stuck.

inference.note: No psychotic features (delusions/hallucinations) and no suicidal ideation reported, which rules out a severe depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (F31.5). The manic episode was brief (4-5 days) but caused significant occupational disruption without hospitalization, consistent with bipolar disorder; current depressive symptoms are pervasive and functionally paralyzing, keeping both moderate and severe (non-psychotic) depressive episode codes as candidates pending further clarification of functional severity.

doctor.intent: Assess severity of depressive functional impairment (e.g., basic self-care) to differentiate moderate vs. severe depressive episode
doctor.question: Over these past three weeks, has the low mood affected your ability to manage basic daily self-care—like eating regular meals, bathing, or getting dressed—or have you still been able to keep up with those things despite feeling low?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: My eating is all over the place—some days I realize at 4 p.m. that I’ve only had coffee, and other nights I stand in the kitchen eating takeout straight from the container even though I’m not really hungry.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's ability to manage self-care, specifically mentioning eating regular meals, which directly corresponds to the patient's symptom of significant changes in appetite and irregular eating habits.

patient.answer:
Basic self-care... yeah, that’s... that’s pretty much gone out the window. I mean, getting dressed? I think I’ve been wearing the same oversized grey sweatpants since Tuesday. Or maybe Monday. Showering just feels like this impossible, monumental task. Just the thought of standing under the water and having to, you know, actually wash my hair and go through the motions... it’s just too much. I just can't bring myself to do it. 

But the eating... my eating is just completely all over the place right now. I used to be so regimented, you know? Meal prep on Sundays, perfectly portioned lunches for the plant so I could eat while reviewing the shift logs. But now, it’s like my body doesn't even know what a normal routine is anymore. Some days, I’ll be lying there on the couch, just paralyzed, staring at the ceiling and listening to that awful refrigerator hum, and I’ll happen to glance at my phone and realize it’s 4 p.m. and I haven’t had a single bite of food. I’ll realize that all I’ve had is coffee. Just... maybe a cup or two of coffee that I forced myself to make in the morning, which usually just end up sitting on the coffee table getting cold anyway. 

And then, it’s like a switch flips, but not in a good way. Other nights, I’ll just... I'll end up ordering a massive amount of Chinese food or something, because the idea of actually turning on the stove or chopping a vegetable is just laughable right now. And when the delivery gets here, I don't even bother getting a plate or sitting down at the table like a normal person. I just stand there, right in the middle of the kitchen, under those terrible fluorescent lights, eating the takeout straight from the container. And the weirdest part is, I’m not even really hungry when I’m doing it. I'm just standing there, mindlessly chewing, staring at the backsplash, while my brain is still just agonizing over the assembly floor and the overtime budget and all the people I let down. It's not about nourishment at all, it's just this mechanical thing I do while I'm trapped in my own head. So, no, regular meals aren't happening. None of it is happening. I can barely manage to keep track of what day it is, let alone actually take care of myself.

inference.note: Manic episode lasted only 4-5 days (less than the 7-day minimum required for F31.3/mania per DSM-IHC criteria used for F31.3 hypomania distinction), but caused marked impairment requiring occupational health intervention, consistent with a full manic episode by severity criteria rather than hypomania. Current depressive episode is severe with marasmus-level self-neglect, psychomotor retardation, and near-complete functional incapacity, but without psychotic features. This supports F31.4 (bipolar disorder, current episode severe depression without psychotic features) over F31.3.

opening_question.intent: Identify the primary reason for the patient's visit today
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a clear manic episode (≥4-7 days of decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, pressured speech, flight of ideas, excessive goal-directed activity, and behavior causing severe occupational impairment requiring workplace intervention) followed immediately by a major depressive episode (3 weeks of depressed mood, anhedonia, psychomotor retardation, guilt, appetite disturbance, self-care neglect) without psychotic features and without active suicidal ideation. This pattern of a full manic episode alternating with a major depressive episode meets criteria for Bipolar I Disorder, and the current episode being depressive without psychotic features corresponds to F31.4.
